KELCEY TIER ROAD RECONSTRUCTION AND SAFETY UPGRADES The section of Kelcey Tier Road between Sherston Road and north of Ellice Hill Drive was declining in condition to a point where rehabilitation was necessary, with 950m of road pavement reconstructed and 470m of corner resurfacing The project also involved safety improvements through seal widening, crest verticle curve improvements, property access alignment and sealing, and stormwater drainage control This project was identified and funded by the Federal Government through the Blackspot Program due to the incident history of the intersection and criteria relating to safety The roundabout construction also involved the realignment of the road kerb and footpaths to provide improved traffic flow and pedestrian access and crossing points THE LEE ROAD RECONSTRUCTION AND UPGRADE The Lee is a small cul-de-sac street providing access to about 20 properties and situated in a low-lying area The road kerb and pavement had deteriorated to a point requiring renewal and upgrade The project involved the installation of sub-soil drainage, upgrade of stormwater inlet pits, replacement of road kerb and resurfacing

Flood Level Monitoring: In partnership with Council's Emergency Management team, rolled out new flood sensors at critical locations, such as the Don River gauge near Buster Road Bridge, Reece High School and the Gatenby Drive detention basins These solar-powered sensors monitor river and basin water levels in real time If water rises rapidly or reaches alert thresholds, automated warnings are sent to Council’s dashboard and emergency responders The system provides early warning of flash floods or overflowing stormwater infrastructure, providing valuable lead time to close roads, deploy pumps, or alert the community This year, five flood cameras and radar units were successfully integrated into Councils central monitoring platform with 24/7 live feeds and automated alerts.
